stages.name: Requirements
stages.entryQuestion: Before designing a ride-hailing service, what scope and scale assumptions would you clarify?
stages.objective: Agree on product behavior, measurable quality targets and the stated exercise workload.

completionCriteria.name: Functional scope
completionCriteria.guidance: Clarify rider/driver actions, cancellation, assignment and payment boundaries; location and matching freshness differ from trip durability.

completionCriteria.name: Quality targets
completionCriteria.guidance: Set matching latency and stale-location limits, and require exclusive assignment despite retries and partitions.

completionCriteria.name: Capacity estimates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use the fictional baseline or state a justified alternative; derive average and peak rates and distinguish payload bytes from replication and indexes.

stages.name: High Level Design
stages.entryQuestion: Walk me through location ingestion, driver search and authoritative trip assignment.
stages.objective: Separate ephemeral geospatial state from durable trip and payment state.

completionCriteria.name: Location boundary
completionCriteria.guidance: Ingest timestamped locations and update a geospatial index with expiry; do not write every fix synchronously to the trip row.

completionCriteria.name: Matching boundary
completionCriteria.guidance: Find eligible candidates and estimate pickup time; nearest straight-line distance alone is not necessarily best.

completionCriteria.name: Trip authority
completionCriteria.guidance: Make a trip service own assignment, state transitions and payment requests in a durable store.

stages.name: Core Flow
stages.entryQuestion: How do you match a rider when nearby drivers can accept other rides at the same time?
stages.objective: Combine geospatial candidate search with concurrency-safe dispatch.

completionCriteria.name: Fresh candidates
completionCriteria.guidance: Use a spatial grid/index or another justified method, filter stale GPS and consider accuracy and road travel time.

completionCriteria.name: Exclusive assignment
completionCriteria.guidance: Use conditional offer reservations and fence stale acceptance. An expiring offer is not an accepted trip: retain authoritative driver ownership for accepted/in-progress trips until a terminal transition or explicit reconciled recovery.

completionCriteria.name: Dispatch retries
completionCriteria.guidance: Handle acceptance timeout, duplicate offers and cancellation while moving to another driver without double booking.

completionCriteria.name: Trip transitions
completionCriteria.guidance: Define legal requested, offered, accepted, in-progress, completed and cancelled transitions.

stages.name: Data Model
stages.entryQuestion: How would you model authoritative trips and assignments separately from live driver locations?
stages.objective: Choose keys for trip history, driver exclusivity and idempotent payment.

completionCriteria.name: Trip schema
completionCriteria.guidance: Store rider, driver, state, state version and timestamps with indexed history access.

completionCriteria.name: Assignment record
completionCriteria.guidance: Track offer expiry separately from durable accepted occupancy, with trip ID and a fencing/version token; enforce at most one nonterminal trip per driver.

completionCriteria.name: Payment request
completionCriteria.guidance: Use a stable payment operation ID and separate payment state from GPS and matching.

stages.name: Reliability
stages.entryQuestion: What happens when GPS is stale, a matching server crashes or payment callbacks are retried?
stages.objective: Preserve assignment safety while allowing bounded degraded behavior.

completionCriteria.name: Stale locations
completionCriteria.guidance: Expire inactive drivers, reject out-of-order fixes and account for GPS uncertainty.

completionCriteria.name: Assignment recovery
completionCriteria.guidance: Expire abandoned offers and fence stale workers; renew or reconcile accepted trip ownership rather than declaring a busy driver available merely because a timer expired.

completionCriteria.name: Payment correctness
completionCriteria.guidance: Use idempotent provider requests and callbacks; trip completion must not charge twice.

stages.name: Scaling
stages.entryQuestion: How would you partition the location and dispatch workload across regions and dense cities?
stages.objective: Scale geospatial reads, hot areas and durable writes independently.

completionCriteria.name: Location capacity
completionCriteria.guidance: 500000 drivers / 5 seconds is 100000 updates/s; a 2x burst is 200000 updates/s. Do not confuse this with trip request throughput.

completionCriteria.name: Regional ownership
completionCriteria.guidance: Partition by city/region and subdivide hot cells while searching neighboring cells and handling boundaries.

completionCriteria.name: Durable throughput
completionCriteria.guidance: Size 231.48 average and 1157.41 peak ride requests/s separately from location traffic; buffer optional history asynchronously.

stages.name: Tradeoffs
stages.entryQuestion: What would you trade between matching quality, latency and assignment consistency during failures?
stages.objective: Defend a concrete regional dispatch policy.

completionCriteria.name: Matching quality tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Compare nearest-candidate dispatch with ETA-aware or batched matching and state a latency budget.

completionCriteria.name: Consistency tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Distinguish eventually fresh locations from exclusive authoritative assignment; explain the partition policy.

completionCriteria.name: Operations tradeoff
completionCriteria.guidance: Choose key health signals such as stale-driver rate, match latency, expired offers and duplicate-payment prevention.
